Main_findings_preserved: Mapped Forge47.4.10 LivingEntity.addEffect first calls virtual canBeAffected; rejection returns false before Added. Default canBeAffected posts Applicable (result ALLOW/DENY overrides default), then undead poison/regeneration fallback. It is not a cancelable Added event.

Added is posted with incoming unmerged instance and old instance before first insertion or update(). Thus merely observing Added is not proof of a changed active effect. The mapped method has no client guard of its own; local/source callers determine side.

MobEffectInstance.update with same type/amplifier, shorter finite duration, same ambient/visible/icon leaves old duration unchanged and returns false. A different presentation flag can independently make update return true; that still does not establish duration replacement.

EffectPresentation.added only marks statusDirty for its eight custom effects. Its later tick/tracking paths check actual hasEffect before sending. This source review does not accuse it of directly sending successful visual state from Added. Vanilla poison is not in its eight-effect list.

QiConstitution DENY concerns YIN/YANG with matching full day/night set, not generic poison. Warm-wine Applicable handler concerns custom FROST, not poison. Template CLOCKWORK_DOG refuses poison/wither/internal injury before super, so those branches bypass the superclass Applicable bus. CORPSE/SKULL return UNDEAD and ordinarily use superclass fallback.

EquipmentBehaviors.effect queues a new incoming duration*3/4 instance on any nonbeneficial finite Added event when ServerPlayer wears >=2cinnabar and shortening flag is false. It does not compare old instance or final native update result.

On END ServerPlayer tick, queued shortening compares only same amplifier and current duration>desired; requests removeEffect then addEffect(desired), ignores both results, under shortening=true to avoid recursive enqueue. It does not bind queued work to the originally observed old/new effect object.

Consequently a rejected shorter same-amplifier refresh can enqueue a much shorter replacement of an existing long effect, although addEffect returned false. This is a bounded source-level counterexample, subject to intervening state and Forge removal/admission hooks, not observed runtime behavior.

Fourcinnabar or active antidote additionally requests poison removal on the local tick; therefore isolated shortening diagnostics should use exactly2cinnabar and a harmful non-poison effect such as weakness to avoid conflating that separate cleanse.

A poison-smoke quest acquisition receipt should remain tied to actual paid full-identity item, while cloud creation, Added, actual effect-map change and subsequent damage/cleanse are distinct facts. None of these source observations creates an acquisition advancement or awards a reward.
